page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-4 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the n4 server family. It features 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation model. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of memory per core. The processor includes an L1d cache of 48 KB, an L2 cache of 2 MB, and an L3 cache of 260 MB. No local storage or GPU accelerators are bundled with this instance, and it does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance profile characterized by average single-core capabilities but weaker multi-core and memory-bound scaling. Single-core performance is average, as demonstrated by a stress-ng single-core score of 1561.99 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1807.0. Conversely, multi-core benchmarks fall into the lower tier, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 3213.05 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 4100.0. Memory bandwidth is also limited, measuring 32.36 GB/sec for large-block reads and 21.01 GB/sec for large-block writes, both of which represent lower-tier performance.

Despite multi-core limitations, the processor supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE, AMX_INT8) for matrix math, alongside cryptography accelerations like AES and SHA_NI. This hardware enablement supports average performance in specific tasks such as CPU encryption and text processing. Static web serving throughput is average at 6.53 GB/sec. The instance is suitable for general-purpose workloads, basic web serving, and lightweight text or cryptographic processing, but is less suited for memory-intensive databases, software compilation, or heavy multi-threaded computing.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-4 is a general-purpose x86_64 server featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs from 2 physical Intel cores and 16.0 GB of RAM. It lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks reveal a distinct split: single-core operations, such as single-threaded gzip compression and Geekbench single-core tasks, perform at an average level, while multi-core and memory-intensive tasks fall into the lower tier. This is evidenced by weak scores in multi-core stress-ng, software compilation, and memory bandwidth. However, the CPU supports advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and Intel AMX, which assist in specific cryptographic and matrix operations. With average static web serving throughput of 6.53 GB/sec, this instance is best suited for lightweight web serving, basic text processing, and general-purpose workloads that do not demand high multi-threaded scaling or massive memory bandwidth.
